rules.statement: When a test can't trigger a platform-specific guard in a script on the CI platform, have it find the guard's block in the script's AST and run that body against a fixture with its variables bound, rather than only checking the guard's text or position with a regex.
rules.why: A text-only check still passes when the guard keeps its wording but passes the wrong argument, misreads a return value or drops details from its error message. Running the body as written catches those mistakes.
rules.check: Look for tests that check a script's guard or branch only by regex or string matching on the source. Running the extracted block against a fixture is the expected alternative, with assertions on when it throws and what its message says.

rules.statement: When a helper treats a failing external command (such as a git subcommand) as 'no problem', fail open only for the specific expected failure and say in a comment that this is deliberate. Report the command's error output for any other failure instead of hiding stderr and returning nothing.
rules.why: Swallowing every non-zero exit makes a corrupt clone or any other git error look like a clean result. The guard then lets the operation go on, and the user hits the obscure downstream error the guard was meant to replace.
rules.check: Look for helpers that redirect an external command's stderr to null and return an empty or 'ok' result on any non-zero exit code, without telling the expected failure apart from others and without a comment that the fail-open is deliberate.
